answer: One workable design: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because orchard only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, violet is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any velvet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
